name: 45 Degree Twisting Hyperextension
instructions: Fix your feet to the footrests and press your thighs against the padded platform.
Place your hands behind your head and lean forward.
Raise yourself by leaning backward and twisting your torso to a side.
Hold for a while, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Perform the twisting motion smoothly and avoid jerking to prevent strain on your back.
Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to maintain stability and support your spine.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift and twist, and inhaling as you lower back down.
description: 45 Degree Twisting Hyperextension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Glutes.

name: Alternate Superman
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended straight in front of you and your legs extended straight back.
Lift your right arm and left leg simultaneously off the floor, engaging your back muscles. Hold briefly.
Lower your right arm and left leg back to the mat.
Lift your left arm and right leg simultaneously off the floor, holding briefly before lowering them back to the mat. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and prevent your lower back from arching excessively.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on lifting your arm and leg to the same height to maintain balance and symmetry.
description: Alternate Superman is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hamstrings.

name: Archer Pull Up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your hands positioned wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull yourself up towards the bar while simultaneously shifting your body to the right, bringing your chest closer to your right hand.
Lower yourself back to the starting position.
Pull yourself up again, this time shifting your body to the left, bringing your chest closer to your left hand. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Focus on using your back muscles rather than relying solely on your arms for the pull-up.
Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement to reduce strain on your joints.
Ensure a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom of each rep and bringing your chest close to the bar at the top.
description: Archer Pull Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended straight to your sides and your legs extended straight behind you.
Lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor, holding the Superman position.
Move your arms in a circular motion, starting from the initial position, sweeping them around straight forward, and back to the starting position.
Continue moving your arms in a controlled, rhythmic manner while maintaining the Superman hold.
tips: Engage your core and glutes to maintain stability and support your lower back throughout the exercise.
Perform the arm movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on keeping your legs and chest lifted off the floor to maintain the Superman hold.
description: Around the World Superman Hold is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hamstrings.

name: Assisted Chin Up Close Grip
instructions: Set the assisted pull-up machine to the support you need and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grip the handles with palms facing you, hands close together.
Pull your chest up toward the handles by driving your elbows down until your chin is above them.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight and repeat.
tips: More counterweight means more help; reduce it as you get stronger.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
description: Assisted Chin Up Close Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with an assisted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms.

name: Bridge - Mountain Climber (Cross Body)
instructions: Begin in a plank position on your toes and hands, with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your left elbow while lightly rotating your hips, stop when your knee passes the elbow.
Return to the starting plank position, then repeat the movement on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure you keep your movements smooth and controlled to maintain form and avoid injury.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you bring your knee towards your elbow and inhaling as you return to the plank position.
Keep your shoulders stable and your core engaged throughout the exercise to enhance effectiveness.
description: Bridge - Mountain Climber (Cross Body) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms raised to shoulder height in front of you, palms facing down.
Lift your right knee towards your left elbow while simultaneously twisting your torso to the right, engaging your core.
Return to the starting position, then lift your left knee towards your right elbow while twisting your torso to the left.
Alternate sides in a controlled manner, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Move smoothly and with control to avoid straining your back or hips.
Ensure your movements are balanced and controlled to prevent injury.
description: High Knee Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

Use your arms for balance.

name: Medicine Ball Hold the World
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a medicine ball above the center of your chest with both hands and your elbows bent.
Press the medicine ball straight upward until your arms are extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping the ball steady.
Bend your elbows and lower the ball toward your chest with control, then repeat.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Press the ball straight upward without moving it toward your head.
Avoid bouncing the ball against your chest.
Inhale as you lower the ball and exhale as you press it upward.
description: Medicine Ball Hold the World is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Forearms.

name: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover
instructions: Lie perpendicular on a bench with only your upper back supported and your hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your core and keep your feet flat on the floor for stability. Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell until your upper arms are in line with your torso or as far as comfortable, feeling a stretch in your chest and lats.
Pull the dumbbell back to the starting position with a controlled motion, keeping your elbows slightly bent. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid letting your elbows flare out; maintain a slight bend throughout the movement.
Ensure your shoulders and upper back remain in contact with the bench throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
description: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

name: Dumbbell Pullover (Bent Arm)
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench, with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, following the same arc as you lowered it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
Ensure your back and shoulders are firmly supported on the bench.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far behind your head to prevent shoulder strain.
description: Dumbbell Pullover (Bent Arm) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

name: Dumbbell Pullover on Floor
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Just before touching the floor, pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to protect your joints.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell back over your chest and inhale as you lower it.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
description: Dumbbell Pullover on Floor is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Begin by lying across a bench, with only your upper back and shoulders supported. Your feet should be flat on the floor, and your hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, following the same arc as you lowered it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
Ensure your upper back and shoulders are firmly supported on the bench.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far behind your head to prevent shoulder strain.
description: Dumbbell Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

name: Arm Crossover Chest Out
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing the floor.
Bring your arms forward while straightening them and cross them in front of your chest twice.
Return your arms to the starting position, extending them out to the sides and bringing your chest forward.
Continue crossing your arms in front of your chest and extending them back out to the sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed to avoid unnecessary tension in your neck and upper back.
Use a mirror to ensure your movements are symmetrical and maintain proper form.
Breathe deeply, exhaling as you cross your arms and inhale as you extend them back out.
description: Arm Crossover Chest Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

name: Arm Double Crossover
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing the floor.
Bring your arms forward while keeping them bent and cross them in front of your chest twice.
Return your arms to the starting position, extending them out to the sides.
Continue crossing your arms in front of your chest and extending them back out to the sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your movements smooth and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Alternate which arm crosses over the other each time to ensure balanced muscle engagement.
Maintain an upright posture and engage your core to support your back and maintain balance.
description: Arm Double Crossover is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

name: Bodyweight Standing Triangle Fly
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands behind your head, forming a triangle with your bent elbows, elbows facing outwards.
Close your elbows together in front of you, bringing them towards each other.
Open your elbows back out to the sides to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and avoid arching your back during the exercise.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid pushing your head forward as you bring your elbows together.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your elbows together.
description: Bodyweight Standing Triangle Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

name: Chest Fly Side Step
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees, and your elbows open wide at shoulder height.
Step your right foot out to the side, bending your right knee slightly as you bring your elbows together in front of you until they are close together and back.
Return to the starting position by stepping your left foot out to the side while repeating the fly motion with your arms.
Repeat the movement alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your arms remain bent at the elbows throughout the chest fly motion.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your elbows together in front of you.
description: Chest Fly Side Step is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

name: Chest Pull Back
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and leaning slightly forward at the hips. Bend your arms in front of your chest with your palms facing each other, lightly squeezing to activate your chest.
Perform a rowing motion with your right arm by pulling it back, bending your elbow, and squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Return your right arm to the starting position, keeping your left arm steady and engaged in front of your chest.
Repeat the rowing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine to maximize the engagement of you back muscles.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to ensure proper muscle activation.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Ensure your chest remains open and engaged by maintaining light tension between your palms.
description: Chest Pull Back is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

name: Band Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the end of a resistance band, with your right hand, anchored under your right foot. Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing up.
Start with your wrist extended down towards the floor, keeping your forearm stationary.
Curl your wrist upward, bringing your knuckles towards your forearm, squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your wrist downwards. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearm stationary on your thighs to isolate the wrist movement.
Focus on squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl your wrists and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
description: Band Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

name: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench
instructions: Kneel in front of a flat bench, holding a barbell with both hands, palms facing down (overhand grip). Rest your forearms on the bench with your wrists hanging over the edge and allow them to hang down.
Curl your wrists upward, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your forearms or upper arms to lift the weight; the movement should come from your wrists.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing them during the exercise.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
description: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Forearms.

name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip (palms facing backward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended, and the barbell should rest against your glutes.
Flex your wrists to curl the barbell upward, bringing the barbell toward your forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, squeezing your forearm muscles.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your arms or shoulders to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
description: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet spread wide apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on the edge of the bench, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist flexors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
description: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible while maintaining control.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist flexors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
description: Barbell Wrist Curl on Knees is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

name: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists relaxed so the barbell hangs as much as possible.
Extend the barbell upward by extending your wrists, raising the barbell as far as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly bring the barbell back to the starting position by relaxing your wrists. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist extensors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you extend the barbell down and inhaling as you curl it back up.
description: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with a straight bar attached to the low pulley. Grasp the bar with both hands using an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just beyond your knees, allowing the bar to hang down.
Curl the bar upwards by flexing your wrists, bringing the bar towards your forearms.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs throughout the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
description: Cable Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

name: Cable Wrist Extension
instructions: Stand sideways, facing away from a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using an underhand grip. Bend your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keep it tucked against your side with your forearm stationary.
Extend your hand at the wrist joint, moving your hand downward while keeping the rest of your arm still. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Curl the weight by flexing at the wrist joint, bringing your hand upward. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Slowly lower your hand back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked against your side throughout the exercise.
Move only at your wrist while keeping your forearm still.

name: Alternate Single Leg Raise Plank
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.

name: Copenhagen Plank
instructions: Lie on your side and rest your forearm on the floor under your shoulder.
Place your top leg on a bench at knee or ankle height, with your bottom leg hanging free underneath.
Press your forearm and top leg down to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, and raise your bottom leg toward the bench.
Hold the position while breathing steadily, then lower your hips with control and switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips stacked; don't let them roll forward or back.
Start with the bench under your knee and progress to the ankle as you get stronger.
description: Copenhagen Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Shoulders, Glutes.

name: Crab Twist Toe Touch
instructions: Begin by sitting on the floor with your legs bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed behind you with your fingers pointing towards your body.
Engage your glutes and press through your palms and feet to lift your hips off the floor, creating a tabletop position with your body.
Simultaneously lift your right hand and left foot off the floor and twist your torso to reach your right hand towards your left foot, attempting to touch your left toe.

Return your hand and leg to the floor and repeat the movement on the opposite side by lifting your left hand and reaching towards your right foot. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the twist with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.

name: Barbell Clean Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out, with a barbell on the floor in front of you. Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, keep your back straight, and your chest up. Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.
As the barbell passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders to bring the barbell to your upper thighs.
Reverse the movement by lowering the barbell back to the floor with control, maintaining a straight back and engaged core. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine to avoid rounding your back and prevent injury.
Use your legs and hips to drive the barbell up, minimizing the strain on your lower back.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift to maintain proper form.

Brace your core and drive through your heels as you extend your knees and hips simultaneously, keeping the barbell close to your legs throughout the lift.
Stand fully upright squeezing your glutes at the top of the exercise. Keep your shoulders back, and the bar resting against your thighs.
Hinge at your hips first, then bend your knees to lower the barbell under control along the same path until it returns to the floor.
tips: Keep the barbell as close to your body as possible throughout the lift and avoid rounding your lower back.
Drive through your heels while extending your hips and keep your chest up.
